providers.title: Second out-neighborhoods as images
providers.scope: In an oriented graph, v is not in F^2({v}), so N_2^+(v) = F^2({v}) minus F({v}).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Closed strong components
providers.scope: Every nonempty finite oriented graph has a strong component with no arc leaving it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Minimal counterexamples are strongly connected
providers.scope: A minimal counterexample has at least two vertices, is strongly connected, and every vertex has an in-neighbor.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Subset deficit (OpenAI, adapting Seacrest)
providers.scope: In a minimal counterexample, |F^2(S) minus F(S)| < |F(S) minus S| for every nonempty proper vertex set S.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Images in a transitive tournament
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The blow-up estimate
providers.scope: In D[T_m], |U| - 2|F(U)| + |F^2(U)| <= m(|F^2(S) minus F(S)| - |F(S) minus S|) + |S minus F(S)| for U with support S.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Strictly concave growth from the subset deficit (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If D has positive in-degrees and the subset deficit and m > n, then D[T_m] has positive in-degrees and |U| + |F^2(U)| < 2|F(U)| for every nonempty proper U.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Reduction (OpenAI)
providers.scope: A counterexample to the second neighborhood conjecture yields a graph with positive in-degrees and strictly concave growth on every nonempty proper vertex set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Berge's augmenting paths
providers.scope: A matching that is not maximum has an augmenting path.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Koenig's theorem
providers.scope: In a finite bipartite graph, the alternating-reachability set of a maximum matching gives a vertex cover of the same size containing no unmatched vertex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Rank and matchings
providers.scope: The rank of a matrix supported on T is at most the largest size of a matching in T.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Determinants of pattern matrices
providers.scope: A square pattern matrix whose variable positions contain a perfect matching has a nonzero determinant polynomial; the same holds for block-diagonal combinations.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Kernels at maximum rank
providers.scope: If D has the largest rank among matrices supported on T, then x_j y_s = 0 for x in ker D, y in ker D^T and (s, j) in T.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Pruning of two families of pairs (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Two families of ordered pairs for any finite relation can be pruned to conflict-free subfamilies, keeping conflict-free members, deleting at most |H| plus the number of uncovered shared points.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Columns and rows of compatible pairs
providers.scope: With positive in-degrees, every column of P and row of Q of a compatible pair containing the diagonal is a nonempty proper vertex set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: No strictly concave growth (OpenAI)
providers.scope: No nonempty finite oriented graph with positive in-degrees has |U| + |F^2(U)| < 2|F(U)| for every nonempty proper U.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex v with |N_1^+(v)| <= |N_2^+(v)|.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Arc-weighted form
providers.scope: For nonnegative arc weights some vertex v has sum_s beta_v(s) >= sum_{u in N_1^+(v)} w(vu).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Vertex-weighted form
providers.scope: For nonnegative vertex weights some vertex v has eta(N_1^+(v)) <= eta(N_2^+(v)).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A theorem of the alternative
providers.scope: If no xi >= 0 has M^T xi < 0 in every coordinate, some probability vector eta has M eta >= 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A balanced weighting
providers.scope: Every nonempty finite oriented graph has a probability weighting with eta(N_1^+(v)) <= eta(N_2^+(v)) at every vertex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Graphs without directed triangles
providers.scope: Without directed triangles some vertex has d^+(v) <= |Z(v)| and n - 1 >= 2 d^+(v) + d^-(v).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Directed triangles from degrees n/3
providers.scope: Minimum in- and out-degree at least n/3 force a directed triangle.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Regular graphs of girth four
providers.scope: An r-regular oriented graph without directed triangles has at least 3r + 1 vertices; the bound is attained.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
